clue.text: Keen crimebuster Eliot wanting to pitch in

parts.note: keen means eager, ready and willing
Eliot Ness was the Prohibition agent who led the Untouchables against Al Capone

explanation.surface: An eager lawman, Eliot of the Untouchables, longs to join in the fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen' looks like the definition but is the first piece; the definition is the gerund phrase at the end, read as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Being eager to pitch in and help is a readiness, the state of being glad to do something.

clue.text: Fictionally just with 19

explanation.definitionFit: Just William is Richmal Crompton's series of children's books; and Prince William is the royal who goes with PRINCE, the answer to 19.

clue.text: Manipulate sound instruction to abandon woman!

indicators.note: the word sound tells us the phrase is heard rather than read, giving a word spoken alike

parts.note: an order to desert a woman is 'leave her!'

explanation.surface: A heartless piece of advice: dump her!
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective on 'instruction' but signals the homophone: 'leave her', said in a non-rhotic accent, matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To lever something is to prise or move it with a bar, working it into position.

clue.text: Worshipful types lost a ride when overturned

indicators.note: overturned suggests the letters of the phrase lost a ride are upset and rearranged

explanation.surface: Churchgoers missed out on a lift after their vehicle tipped over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' is the anagram signal on LOST A RIDE; 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Idolaters are people who worship idols, a kind of worshipper.

clue.text: Biblical interpretation is following former example directions

parts.note: ex- means former, as in ex-wife
e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: Interpreting scripture means following the pattern of earlier teachers and guidance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' looks like 'after' in time but sets the word 'is' at the end of the answer; 'directions' supplies two compass points at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Exegesis is the critical explanation of a text, especially scripture.

clue.text: Leader is depressed and consumed out east

parts.note: depressed means sad

indicators.note: out tells us a letter, the abbreviation for east, is dropped from the word for consumed

parts.note: consumed means ate, as of a meal
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A head of state is feeling low after eating, then heads off eastwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes E from ATE, leaving AT. Anwar Sadat was President of Egypt.
explanation.definitionFit: Anwar Sadat was President of Egypt from 1970 to 1981, a national head of state.

clue.text: Excuse before the reading matter

parts.note: pre- is a prefix meaning before
the text is the written matter to be read

explanation.surface: An apology offered ahead of the written material.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretext is a false reason given to cover the real one, a cover story.

clue.text: Pens abbey

explanation.definitionFit: Fountain pens are a kind of writing instrument; Fountains Abbey is a ruined Cistercian monastery in Yorkshire.

clue.text: Greenwood classic has nothing out of work

parts.note: love means nothing, the zero score in tennis
on the dole is British slang for claiming unemployment benefit, so jobless

explanation.walkthrough: Walter Greenwood's 1933 novel of Depression-era Salford. 'The dole' is British unemployment benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: Walter Greenwood wrote this 1933 novel about poverty and unemployment in Salford.

clue.text: Idle fellow on bagpipe?

explanation.definitionFit: A drone is a lazy person living off others, like the male bee; and it is a bagpipe's pipe sounding one sustained note.

clue.text: Encroachment where cat's-eyes seen!

explanation.definitionFit: An inroad is an intrusion into territory; cat's-eyes are reflective studs set in a road surface, so they are found in the road.

clue.text: Punishment will come to a stop

explanation.definitionFit: A sentence is the penalty a court imposes; a written sentence ends with a full stop.

clue.text: Deer and French firearm

parts.note: the musk deer is a small Asian deer prized for its scent gland
et is the French for and

explanation.surface: A stag and a French gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A musket is an old smooth-bore shoulder gun.

clue.text: Anger about in set of successful corporal

indicators.note: in means the jumbled letters sit within the other word

parts.note: set is given as written

indicators.note: about here signals the letters of anger are turned around and mixed up

explanation.surface: Fury over a promoted soldier's place in the ranks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges the word anger to RGEAN, and 'in' sets those letters within the three-letter word, so the outer word is split after its second letter. A corporal who is successful earns promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: A corporal who wins promotion becomes the next rank up, a sergeant.

clue.text: On 'ead with skill in transportation

parts.note: what grows on the head is hair, and dropping its h in Cockney style, matching 'ead, gives 'air
craft means skill

explanation.surface: Cockney talk of a head with a knack for getting around.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'ead tells you to drop the H from the word too, as a Cockney speaker would.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft is a flying machine, a means of transport.

clue.text: Animal for arranged short race?

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of short race are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Which beast would be put in for a sprint?
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges SHORT RACE; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A carthorse is a heavy draught horse, a working animal.

clue.text: Nothing in river that quietly flows out of Latvian city, dance

parts.note: Riga is the capital of Latvia

indicators.note: in puts the zero sign inside the river's name

parts.note: Sholokhov's novel And Quiet Flows the Don names the Russian river Don

explanation.definitionFit: A rigadoon is a lively Provençal dance for couples.

clue.text: Aristocracy of Middlesex cricket that's trendy

hip means fashionable

explanation.walkthrough: LORD'S is the London cricket ground where Middlesex play.
explanation.definitionFit: A lordship is the rank or dignity of a lord, a noble title.

clue.text: Cattle I herd through the window

explanation.surface: A farmer drives livestock past the window.
explanation.walkthrough: 'herd' rearranges CATTLE I; 'through the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A lattice window has small panes set in a crisscross framework of lead strips.

clue.text: Indefinite number in cost above 18

indicators.note: in places the symbol for an unknown number inside the word for cost

parts.note: cost means price
n is the algebraic symbol for an unspecified number

explanation.surface: An unknown figure in a price that outranks nobility.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 is LORDSHIP: a prince ranks higher than a lord.
explanation.definitionFit: In the peerage a royal heir outranks any lord.

clue.text: Messy arrangement with a graduate in national residence
